name: Machine Seated Calf Raise
summary: An isolation exercise performed on a seated calf machine that emphasizes the soleus muscle through controlled plantarflexion.

setup: Sit on the machine with the balls of your feet positioned on the foot bar, hip-width apart, and your heels hanging freely off the edge.
Adjust the thigh pad so it rests snugly over the lower part of your quadriceps, just above your knees.
Disengage the safety latch by pushing up onto your toes and pivoting the release lever out of the way.
steps: Slowly lower your heels toward the floor under control until you feel a deep stretch in the Achilles tendon and lower calf.
Pause briefly in the stretched position without bouncing.
Press firmly through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible into full plantarflexion.
Contract the calf muscles hard at the peak for a brief second before initiating the next descent.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you lower your heels into the stretch; exhale as you push up onto the balls of your feet.
cues: Pause and squeeze at the peak

common_faults.fault: Bouncing out of the bottom of the movement using Achilles tendon elasticity.
common_faults.correction: Pause for one full second at the bottom of the stretch to eliminate the stretch reflex and force muscular recruitment.

common_faults.fault: Using partial range of motion by not fully lowering or raising the heels.
common_faults.correction: Lower the weight to ensure full dorsiflexion and drive all the way onto the balls of your feet at the top.

common_faults.fault: Placing the thigh pads too high on the femur, causing leverage disadvantage and sliding.
common_faults.correction: Position the pads directly across the lower thighs just above the kneecaps.

precautions: Ensure the safety catch is securely engaged before stepping out of the machine.
